To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microbiota is a key regulator of the gut–brain and brain–gut axis and that the microbiota–brain axis is a new concept that will contribute to our understanding of how the brain influences the immune system, which in turn influences the microbiota.
the gut microbiota and the gut–brain communication are two major players in the regulation of brain function.
the brain and the microbiota are intimately related and that this relationship can be manipulated in order to treat human diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how gut bacteria and the brain interact, and the clinical relevance of this interaction.
how the brain and the gut interact with the microbiota, and how this interaction is involved in the development of human disease states.
the gut–brain microbiota axis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain–gut microbiota axis is a complex and multifaceted entity that is only beginning to be understood.
the microbiota is a major determinant of the brain, which in turn is a major determinant in the microbiota.
the microbiota–immune–gut–neural axis is a complex system that is still not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiome is a key component of the gut–brain communication system.
the gut microbiota is an important player in the gut–brain–microbiota axis.
the microbiota–immune–neural axis has a profound impact on the development and function of our brain and behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are at the beginning of a new paradigm in the field of medicine that is based upon the concept of a microbiome–host axis that will be of relevance to all areas of human health.
the microbiota and the brain are not isolated from each other.
the microbiota–brain axis is not only relevant to psychiatric conditions but also to the immune and inflammatory systems.
